title: Magnetism Adventure 2 · Calculations
welcome_lead: Now electricity meets magnetism — solenoids, electromagnets and the force on a current-carrying wire. 🧭
meta_desc: Magnetism Adventure 2 — GCSE Physics on solenoids, electromagnets, the motor effect F=BIL and Fleming's left-hand rule.
final_note: You used F = B × I × L, applied Fleming's left-hand rule and saw how solenoids make strong electromagnets.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Wrap a wire into a coil and pass a current through it — you get a solenoid. 🧭

Inside, the field is strong and uniform. Outside, it looks like a bar magnet's field.

Add an iron core and you have an electromagnet — much stronger, and switchable with the current.

A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force. This is the motor effect.

The size of the force is given by F = B × I × L. F is in newtons (N), B in tesla (T), I in amperes (A), L in metres (m).

The force is largest when the wire is at 90° to the field. Parallel to the field, the force is zero.

Use your left hand for motors. Hold thumb, first finger and second finger at right angles.

First finger = magnetic Field (N to S). Second finger = conventional Current (+ to −). Thumb = the Force / motion.

Reverse the current OR flip the magnet to reverse the force. Do both — and the force goes back the same way.

mcqs.q: How can you make an electromagnet stronger? (Best single change.)
options: Use a wooden core
Add an iron core
Use less current
Unwind the coils

mcqs.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the first finger represent?
options: Force
Current
Magnetic field
Voltage

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.
